newsitem.title: USA: Investors scoop up $2.7 bln US corp debt, more seen.
newsitem.headline: Investors scoop up $2.7 bln US corp debt, more seen.

text.p: Investors scooped up close to $2.7 billion in new straight corporate debt issues on Wednesday, but still a boatload of new supply is about to be dumped on the market, dealers said.
"Names just keep pouring into the market and deals continue to be well received," said one high-grade syndicate source. "Expect some more to hit the market today," he added.
On Thursday, Commercial Credit set $200 million in 6.20 percent A1/A-plus rated five-year notes to yield 35 basis points over Treasuries via JP Morgan Securities.
Meanwhile, Millennium America Inc is set to bring its $750 million two-part debt offering via Goldman Sachs & Co.

The deal is expected to consist of $500 million in 10-year notes, with price talk seen in the 85 to 88 basis points area, and $250 million in 30-year senior debentures with price talk seen between 115 to 118 basis points over Treasuries.
Also, Circus Circus Enterprises is in line to issue $300 million of debt in its own two-part debt offering.
The first tranche is expected to consist of $150 million in 100-year bonds which are puttable in the seventh year via Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, sources said.
The second tranche is for $150 million in 40-year bonds with a put option in the 12th year via underwriter Goldman Sachs & Co Inc.

The Las Vegas-based company said it intends to use the proceeds from the sale of the debt for general corporate purposes, which may include acquisitions, capital expenditures and repurchases of shares of the company's common stock.
ABN Amro Bank NV is still expected to come to market with $300 million in AA2/AA-minus rated 30-year debt, sources said.
Also, Smith Barney is expected to underwrite a $200 million 30-year deal for TransContinental Gas Pipeline.

In other upcoming issues, syndicate sources said on Thursday that Enersis SA's initial debt offering for $500 million in Baa1/A-minus debt may be bumped up in size by another $250 million with the addition of another tranche.
In other deals, Peoples Bank Corp may tap the market with a $150 million 10-year debt issue via Lehman Brothers.
Also, sources said Simon DeBartolo may tap the market with $200 million in 10-year debt via Merrill Lynch.
Dealers said on Wednesday close to $2.0 billion in investment-grade debt priced in the corporate bond primary market.
Among Wednesday's issuers were TransAmerica Finance, Wisconsin Bell, Hertz Corp, Oasis Residential, Royal Bank of Canada, Xerox Corp, Rubbermaid Inc and BankAmerica.
Dealers said new issues were met with good demand and Rubbbermaid's 10-year debt offering, twice oversubscribed, met with more demand in secondary trading.
"Rubbermaid is issue plus bid in secondary trading...players were willing to pay an eighth over the issue price for it," one syndicate source said.

Another $700 million was priced on Wednesday in the 144A private placement debt arena. Among the issuers were Aristech Chemicals, Phoenix Home Life, Peterson Publishing, The William Carter Co and Ryder TRS Inc.
Still, another $2.0 billion in 144A debt offering are slated to come to market, dealers added.
Newport News Shipbuilding & Dry Dock Co, a unit of Tenneco Inc, is expected to price a $400 million two-part debt offering via JP Morgan Securities.
The first tranche is expected to consist of $200 million in 10-year senior notes and the second tranche consist of $200 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes, sources said.
Tevecap SA is expected to tap the private placement market with $225 million in 144A senior notes due 2004 via Chase Securities. Price talk on the issue is 12.625 percent.
HS Resources Inc is expected to issue $125 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via Salomon Brothers. Price talk is in the 325 basis points arena.
Atrium Cos is expected to issue $100 million in 144A 10-year senior subordinated notes via BT Securities, sources said.
Eastern Energy Ltd is also expected to issue $300 million in 10-year 144A debt via Merrill Lynch.
Also, WCI Steel is expected to tap the market with a $300 million 10-year senior secured note deal via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities. Price talk is in the 9.875 percent area.
Hawk Corp is expected to bring $100 million in 144A notes due 2003 with price talk in the 10.25 to 10.50 percent range, sources said.
Clark Material Handling Corp is expected to issue $120 million in 10-year senior notes via Jefferies Inc. Price talk is seen at 10.75 to 11.0 percent.
Lamar Advertising is expected to issue $225 million in B1/B rated 10-year senior subordinated notes via Smith Barney. Price talk is in the 9.625 percent arena.
Off the calendar is Cable Plus Holdings' $150 million in 10-year 144A notes which has been postponed, according to underwriter Goldman Sachs & Co.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
